question.problem:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

$$
F(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1\text{ or }y<1 \\ \frac{4({x}^{2}-1)(y-1)}{9y}, & 1\le x\le 2,\,1\le y\le 4 \\ {F}_{X}(x), & 1\le x\le 2,\,y>4 \\ {F}_{Y}(y), & x>2,\,1\le y\le 4 \\ 1, & x>2,\,y>4.\end{aligned}
$$

where ${F}_{X}$ and ${F}_{Y}$ are the marginal CDFs of $X$ and $Y,$ respectively. Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $1\le x\le 2$ and $1\le y\le 4.$
question.worked_solution:
Since the partial derivatives of $F(x,y)$ are defined, the joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ is determined by

$$
f(x,y)=\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂x∂y}F(x,y).
$$

For $1\le x\le 2$ and $1\le y\le 4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =\frac{{∂}^{2}}{∂x∂y}F(x,y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{4({x}^{2}-1)(y-1)}{9y})) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4({x}^{2}-1)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{9}-\frac{1}{9y})) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4({x}^{2}-1)\cdot \frac{1}{9{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{4}{9{y}^{2}}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-1) \\  & =\frac{8x}{9{y}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Otherwise, $f(x,y)=0.$
Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{8x}{9{y}^{2}}, & 1\le x\le 2,\,1\le y\le 4 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
